items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The other musicians were ... Emil Christian, a white trombone player ... We passed through Switzerland ... arrived in Venice ... that was where the trip started to get interesting.

ctx.x: Before my departure, we had a recording session with Willie Lewis's band the 15th of October 1936.

Leon Abbey had gone to Chicago and came back with a tenor player named Antony Cosey. The 21st of October we left Paris for Venice, Italy where we took a boat for India. The other musicians were Arthur Lanier, alto and singer, Ollie Tines, drummer, Emil Christian, a white trombone player who had played with the Original Dixieland Band and had lived in England and France a few years. The pianist was Charlie Lewis who had come to Europe with Leon.

We passed through Switzerland which was a beautiful country and arrived in Venice the 22nd of October and that was where the trip started to get interesting. I had read some of the history of Venice and its canals and it says that there is no other city like Venice. We went from the railroad station to the pier by taxi gondolas and watched the way the gondolier guided the gondola and the traffic on the canals. It was a real sight to see. From the pier there was a launch that took us to the ship we were to sail…
